text:
Alex: quick async standup — 2026-03-18

Done: merged emergency kv-evict hotfix (PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/482). Turned on a temporary alert mute for eu-west spike.
Blockers: seeing intermittent 503s from batcher when backlog > ~180. Need more traces (KV cache hit rate looks OK).
Today: writing autoscaler cooldown change (30s → 90s) and a small canary in ap-south-1; will open PR and ping for review.

Maya: thanks — noted for handover. I'll pick up the oncall tonight. Can you drop the link to the query that shows the 503 spike?

Alex: sure — Li ran the query, past 20m trend is here:
```
sum(rate(batcher_503_total[5m])) by (region)
```
Region-level spike mostly in eu-west; I've pasted a small trace id: trace/0x9c3f in the incident span.

Li: posted logs to the incident doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/EVT-174. The spike correlates with a sudden increase in long-tail requests from a specific customer key. Also saw increased GC pause metrics on the batcher pods.

Omar: I'll review the autoscaler PR when it's up. If the GC is the culprit we should try a live heap dump on the canary and rotate the JVM flags. cc @Maya

Maya: ack. I'll schedule the canary smoke test at 15:30 UTC and watch p95/p99. If I see the 503s I can flip a temporary rollover to a fallback model pool.

deploy-bot: canary rollout started for infra/autoscaler change in ap-south-1 — canary id c-20260318-9 — watching error budget.

Alex: great, thanks team. If anyone sees regression in token cost for that model route, ping me. I'll post the PR link shortly. :thumbsup:

Maya: :eyes: will do. Also leaving a quick TODO to add a short eval against our synthetic traffic to catch the long-tail path.
